label: Mailbox (IMAP/SMTP)
terms_note: Open standard, no vendor gate: any host that allows an app password or SASL / XOAUTH2 login. IMAP4rev2 (RFC 9051): implicit TLS on 993 or STARTTLS on 143; AUTHENTICATE with SASL (PLAIN mandatory, SCRAM-SHA-256 recommended); SELECT / FETCH / SEARCH / STORE / APPEND / MOVE / UID; UIDVALIDITY (32-bit, must increase when UIDs are regenerated → resync the cursor); IDLE gives in-connection notifications only — no webhooks, the suite polls / re-issues IDLE. Provider-side sending limits (e.g. Workspace 2,000/day) still apply; the terms of each mailbox provider govern automation.

tools.name: send
tools.endpoint: SMTP submission (RFC 6409, port 587 STARTTLS / 465 implicit TLS)

reference.limits: - `UIDVALIDITY` is a 32-bit value that MUST increase when UIDs are regenerated → the client resets its cursor when it changes (implemented). - RFC 9051 defines **no push / webhook**; IDLE notifies only the open connection → the scheduler polls. - Provider terms and sending caps apply (e.g. Workspace / Outlook daily limits); automated bulk sending through a personal mailbox is where deliverability breaks — the suite's complaint / bounce pause gates still apply. - Thread by `References` / `In-Reply-To` / `Message-ID` only (never sender + subject) — messaging.md rule.

reason: IMAP4rev2 and SMTP are stateful TCP protocols, not HTTP: IMAP is a tagged command/response session over implicit TLS on 993 or STARTTLS on 143 (LOGIN / AUTHENTICATE, SELECT, UID FETCH / SEARCH / STORE; https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9051, re-read 2026-09-25) and SMTP submission is a MAIL FROM / RCPT TO / DATA dialogue on 465/587 (RFC 6409). Remaining gap: an IMAP/SMTP protocol client transport (TLS socket sessions); every runtime capability, including all 2026-09-25 additions, issues HTTPS requests only.
